$comment: Single declaration of what counts as bypassing local commit verification, read by ops/autonomy/verification_bypass_gate.py (which denies it at PreToolUse), by ops/scripts/validate_commit_verification_contract.py (which proves the session briefing and the tracked tree agree with it), and by tests/ops/autonomy/test_verification_bypass_gate.py. Prose that merely says 'never --no-verify' is not enforcement: before this contract every form below was ALLOWED by the gate while eight skill files forbade it. Add a form here and every consumer picks it up; there is nowhere else to state it.
rationale: Pre-commit hooks are the last check that runs before history is written. A hook that can be skipped on the commit that most needs it is decoration. The hooks are also the only gate that sees a change BEFORE it becomes a commit others build on, so a bypass is not deferred work: it is work that silently never happens.
remedy: Fix what the hook reported. A hook failure is evidence (rule 95): diagnose it as a product, test, fixture, environment, or flake defect and repair the narrowest true cause. If the hook itself is wrong, repair the hook in its own commit. If the failure is genuinely unrelated and unfixable in this scope, record it with ops/autonomy/session_debt.py and say so — never skip the hook to move on.

breakglass.note: Human/ops only. An agent MUST NOT set this for itself: exporting it inside the same turn that runs the commit is the bypass, one level up.

git_value_flags.$comment: Flags whose value is a SEPARATE word, so a scanner must skip that word before reading the next flag. Without this, `git commit -m -n` (a message of '-n') reads as a bypass. Flags taking an attached-only optional value (-uno, -S<key>, --cleanup=<mode>) are deliberately absent: they never consume the next word.

forms.label: git commit --no-verify
forms.why: skips every pre-commit and commit-msg hook for this commit, which is the entire local verification plane

forms.$comment: No short form: `git push -n` is --dry-run, which is read-only and must stay allowed.
forms.label: git push --no-verify
forms.why: skips pre-push hooks, the last check before the work leaves the machine

forms.label: git -c core.hooksPath=… <command>
forms.why: repoints the hook directory for this invocation, disabling every hook without naming --no-verify

forms.label: git config core.hooksPath …
forms.why: durably repoints the hook directory, so every later commit in this clone is unverified

forms.$comment: Scoped to a git commit/push segment on purpose. `SKIP=<ids> pre-commit run` is how ops/scripts/run_pr_precommit.sh legitimately narrows the sanctioned gate, and must not be caught here.
forms.label: hook-suppressing environment variable on a git commit/push
forms.why: disables hooks through the environment instead of a flag; the commit is just as unverified

forms.head: pre-commit
forms.label: pre-commit uninstall
forms.why: removes the hook shim from the clone, so verification stops for every later commit, not just this one

forms.label: removing, replacing, or disarming a file under .git/hooks/
forms.why: the durable form of the same bypass: no flag is ever needed again

briefing_lines: `git commit --no-verify` / `-n`, `git push --no-verify`, `core.hooksPath` overrides, hook-suppressing env vars (`SKIP=`, `HUSKY=0`), `pre-commit uninstall`, and edits to `.git/hooks/**` are DENIED at PreToolUse by `ops/autonomy/verification_bypass_gate.py`. Declaration: `ops/config/commit-verification-contract.json`.

A failing hook is evidence, not an obstacle: repair the narrowest true cause (rule 95), or record it with `session_debt.py`. Do not reach for a bypass when a hook fails — there is no form of it that this gate allows.
